findings.summary: The edge-only headers sample claims both `CDN-Cache-Control` and `Cache-Control` are stripped before the client sees them, but `Cache-Control` is exactly the header that must reach the browser for the stated split to work.
findings.evidence: "CDN-Cache-Control: max-age=86400  # edge: 1d" / "Cache-Control: max-age=60         # browser" / "# both stripped before the client sees them" — immediately followed by "Edge 1 day, browser 60s — no custom CDN rule needed".
findings.fix: Change the comment to reflect reality: the CDN consumes the targeted header and forwards `Cache-Control` untouched. E.g. `# CDN consumes the first line; Cache-Control goes to the browser`. If the intent was to show a header the client never sees, use `Surrogate-Control` (Fastly removes it before delivery) — `CDN-Cache-Control` is generally passed through by Cloudflare, so "stripped" is not safe to assert for it either.

findings.summary: The "3. The One-Page Sheet" table is wider than its card and its Header column is clipped by the right page edge.
findings.evidence: Hashed-asset row reads "public, max-age=31536000, im" (cut mid-word before "immutable") and the API GET row reads "private, no-cache + ETag" with the text and table rules running past the card border off the right edge of the page.
findings.fix: Constrain the table to the card width (table-layout: fixed with the Header cell wrapping / word-break on long header values) so both rows wrap onto a second line inside the card instead of overflowing the page.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a part label rather than a hook, so the scroll-stopping line is buried in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of HTTP CACHING FIELD HANDBOOK. Your app is probably fast for the wrong reason — and stale for a reason nobody wrote down."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and demote the label: "Your app is probably fast for the wrong reason — and stale for a reason nobody wrote down. Part 2 of HTTP CACHING FIELD HANDBOOK: 10 pages on how HTTP caching actually works..."

findings.summary: The stated header precedence ranks `CDN-Cache-Control` above `Surrogate-Control` and asserts CDNs honour that order exactly, but RFC 9213 leaves the order to each cache and Fastly evaluates `Surrogate-Control` first.
findings.evidence: "Order: `CDN-Cache-Control` > `Surrogate-Control` > `s-maxage` > `max-age`" / "Well-behaved CDNs honour this precedence exactly". Fastly documents its order of preference as Surrogate-Control, then `Cache-Control: s-maxage`, then `max-age`, then `Expires`, and targets Surrogate-Control before Cache-Control; RFC 9213 says each cache defines its own ordered target list (a CDN-specific field such as `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` outranks `CDN-Cache-Control`).
findings.fix: Rewrite as vendor-dependent: "Typical order: vendor field (e.g. `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control`) > `CDN-Cache-Control` > `Surrogate-Control` > `s-maxage` > `max-age` — but RFC 9213 lets each cache define its own target list; Fastly checks `Surrogate-Control` first. Verify against your CDN's docs." Drop "honour this precedence exactly".

findings.summary: Page 1 asserts hit ratio is the sole success metric, which page 3 then explicitly contradicts, leaving the learner with two opposed rules and no reconciliation.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "A miss pays both — hit ratio is the whole game" vs. page 3: "Hit ratio is not the goal — offload and p99 are" and "99% on tiny assets hides one hot uncached HTML route".
findings.fix: Replace the page 1 bullet with a neutral framing of the miss cost (e.g. "A miss pays both — that gap is what tiering exists to shrink") and let page 3 be the only page that rules on which metric to optimise.

findings.summary: The Edge-Only Headers code block says both shown headers are stripped before the browser, which is false for `Cache-Control` and contradicts the bullet directly beneath it.
findings.evidence: Code: "CDN-Cache-Control: max-age=86400  # edge: 1d" / "Cache-Control: max-age=60         # browser" / "# both stripped before the client sees them" — followed by the bullet "Edge 1 day, browser 60s — no custom CDN rule needed".
findings.fix: Change the comment to name only the edge headers, e.g. "# CDN-Cache-Control is stripped at the edge; Cache-Control reaches the browser".

findings.summary: Section 5's heading is stranded alone at the bottom of page 3 while its body cards flow onto page 4 without a heading.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ends with the bare heading card "5. Hit-Rate Killers" followed by roughly a third of a page of empty corkboard; page 4's top-left card begins mid-list with "• Forgetting Vary: Accept-Encoding — undecodable bodies" and no heading above it.
findings.fix: Keep heading cards with at least their first body card when paginating (treat heading+first block as an unbreakable unit), pushing "5. Hit-Rate Killers" onto page 4 above its bullets.

findings.summary: Page 3 ends on the bare heading "Hit-Rate Killers" with no content under it, and its bullets open page 4 with no heading, so neither page reads as a complete section.
findings.evidence: Page 3 final block: {"type":"heading","text":"Hit-Rate Killers","ink":"red"} with no following block; page 4 opens with "Forgetting `Vary: Accept-Encoding` — undecodable bodies" under the page title "Common Mistakes + Cheat Sheet".
findings.fix: Move the "Hit-Rate Killers" heading to the top of page 4 so it sits directly above its four bullets, and end page 3 on the "Correctness Breakers" bullets.

findings.summary: The service-worker sidebox says omitting `skipWaiting`/`clients.claim` leaves a "stale app forever", but a waiting worker activates on its own once every client controlled by the old worker is gone.
findings.fix: State the actual lifecycle: "No `skipWaiting`/`clients.claim` = new version waits until every tab is closed — an SPA users never fully close stays stale for days."

findings.summary: `Surrogate-Control` appears inside the edge-header precedence chain without ever being introduced as an edge-only header.
findings.evidence: "Order: `CDN-Cache-Control` > `Surrogate-Control` > `s-maxage` > `max-age`" — `Surrogate-Control` appears nowhere else in the part, and the code block above shows only `CDN-Cache-Control` and `Cache-Control`.
findings.fix: Add a bullet before the precedence line naming both edge-only headers, e.g. "`CDN-Cache-Control` and `Surrogate-Control` are edge-only; the CDN reads them and strips them".

findings.summary: The acronym "PoP" is used in a heading and bullets on first appearance in the part and is never expanded.
findings.evidence: Heading "What A PoP Buys" followed by "A CDN is a shared cache with PoPs near users".
findings.fix: Expand on first use: "A CDN is a shared cache with PoPs (points of presence) near users".

findings.summary: "ESI" is introduced as a technique in a single bullet with no expansion and no example of what hole-punching looks like.
findings.evidence: "ESI / edge fragments cache the shell, hole-punch personal parts" — the acronym appears once in the part with no definition.
findings.fix: Expand the acronym and anchor it with a concrete shape, e.g. "ESI (Edge Side Includes): cache the shell, fetch `/header/user` per request".

findings.summary: The heading "Three Ways To Say No" sits above a four-item list, so `private` reads as a fourth way to refuse caching when the callout beneath says it is not.
findings.evidence: Heading "Three Ways To Say No" over bullets "`no-store`…", "`no-cache`…", "`max-age=0`…", "`private` still writes to the user's own disk", then the callout "private is not no-store".
findings.fix: Drop the `private` bullet from that list (the callout already carries it) or split it into its own block below the three.
